reasons: Party mapping is correct: IBM is the Customer/Buyer in this outsourcing arrangement, and Section 9.0(f) is a restriction binding our party, so NOSOLICIT is the right rule to apply.

The cited text substantively supports the compliant/fallback classification on the material terms: scope is limited to the finite 'Transferred Employees' group rather than all Vendor personnel; the covenant is solicitation-only with no no-hire (IBM may hire those who approach it or respond to advertising); and both carve-outs (unsolicited own-initiative contact and general employment advertising/independent search firms) are expressly present.

The two failed deterministic checks are heuristic misses rather than substance: the general-solicitation carve-out is plainly in the text ('by using general employment advertising or communications or independent search firms'), and the duration check failed only because the term is redacted ('[*] years'), not because the clause is silent.
No redline or comment is expected for a compliant finding, and none was proposed — consistent with the playbook's instruction not to redline a clause sitting at the fallback.

Caveat noted and correctly handled in the rationale rather than raised as a deviation: the covenant is one-way and runs a redacted number of 'years' from the Effective Date (plural wording suggests it may exceed 12 months). Since the number is redacted, deviation cannot be asserted; the recommendation to confirm on the unredacted copy that it does not exceed 24 months (walk-away) is the appropriate follow-up.
